clue.text: Advertising campaign for the movement

parts.note: pro is Latin for 'for', as in arguments pro and con
a motion is a movement, as of a hand or body

explanation.surface: A publicity drive is launched on behalf of a political cause.
explanation.definitionFit: A promotion is a publicity push to boost sales of a product.

clue.text: Fruit is gathered in the fall

indicators.note: the little word is gathered up inside the word for what falls from clouds

parts.note: rain is what falls from the sky, a fall of water
taken as written

explanation.surface: Fruit is harvested during the autumn, which Americans call the fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The fall' suggests autumn, the harvest season, but here it is rainfall.
explanation.definitionFit: A raisin is a dried grape, a kind of dried fruit.

clue.text: Second in importance

explanation.surface: Something ranks just below the top in significance.
explanation.definitionFit: Wait a second means wait a short while, an instant; a matter of great moment is one of great weight or significance.

clue.text: Lets out American imprisoned in brawl

indicators.note: the abbreviation for American is shut up inside the jumbled letters
out suggests the letters of the word lets are put out of order

parts.note: US is the usual abbreviation for American, as in United States

explanation.surface: Someone frees a US citizen who was jailed after a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' makes TSLE from LETS, and 'imprisoned in' puts US inside it after the T.
explanation.definitionFit: A tussle is a vigorous scuffle or fight, the same as a brawl.

clue.text: Rages on about wild animals

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters of rages on are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone keeps ranting on the subject of untamed beasts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges the letters of RAGES ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Onagers are wild asses of central Asia, untamed beasts.

clue.text: Soft grain, inferior but still highly esteemed

parts.note: p, for piano, is the musical direction meaning soft
rice is a cereal grain
less can mean lower in rank or worth, as in no less a person

explanation.surface: Some cheap mushy cereal is nonetheless treasured.
explanation.walkthrough: P is the musical marking for soft (piano). 'but still' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Something priceless is beyond any valuation, so it is treasured enormously.

clue.text: Reading for the daily help

parts.note: a daily is a newspaper published every day, a paper
to back someone is to support or help them

explanation.surface: Something to read for the cleaner who comes in each day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The daily help' looks like a British cleaner (a 'daily'), but 'the daily' is a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A paperback is a soft-covered book, light reading matter.

clue.text: Tease by putting salt in tea

indicators.note: putting the words together and rearranging them signals a mixing of the letters

explanation.surface: Someone plays a mean trick on another by adding salt to their cuppa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting' rearranges all the letters of SALT IN TEA.
explanation.definitionFit: To tantalise is to torment with something desired but kept out of reach, a cruel teasing.

clue.text: Mistakes set back a sailor in time

indicators.note: in places the turned sailor inside the word for a period

parts.note: an era is a period of time

indicators.note: set back means the word for a sailor is written backwards

parts.note: a tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: Errors held back a seaman during some period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set back' turns TAR into RAT, which goes 'in' ERA after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata are errors, especially printing errors listed for correction.

clue.text: Notice result of successful appeal

explanation.surface: A sign is the outcome of a winning legal challenge.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the fielding side appeals to the umpire ('Howzat?'); if it succeeds, the batsman is out.
explanation.definitionFit: Being given notice means being sacked from a job; a batsman is given out when the umpire upholds the bowler's appeal.

clue.text: Possibly a grave sign of stress

explanation.surface: A tombstone might mark someone's anxiety.
explanation.walkthrough: A grave is one type of written mark over a vowel, as in à; the definition's 'Possibly' says it is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A grave is one kind of diacritical mark; emphasis on a syllable in speech is also called this.

clue.text: He may be flagging in his duties

definitions.text: He may be flagging in his duties

parts.words: He may be flagging in his duties
parts.note: flagging looks like tiring, but it means waving flags to send messages, as a railway or naval worker does

explanation.surface: A worker is growing tired on the job.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who communicates by waving flags or lamps, as on a railway or ship.

clue.text: Make ball go round like a sphere

indicators.note: round means the letters of ball and go are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: Get a ball rolling in a circle, as balls do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' rearranges BALL GO; 'Make' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Global literally means shaped like a globe, that is, round like an orb.

clue.text: Trying time for a beginner

parts.note: trying looks like difficult, but it means testing: a newcomer serves a trial period

explanation.surface: A newcomer has a hard time at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial period during which a new worker or offender is assessed.

clue.text: I grasp one form of foreign capital

indicators.note: a form of the words means their letters reshaped into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone claims to understand one kind of overseas money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form of' rearranges I GRASP ONE. 'Capital' looks like money but is a city.
explanation.definitionFit: The city-state's chief city shares its name and is a capital in Asia.

clue.text: It provides liquor we imbibe at home with the papers

indicators.note: to imbibe is to take in, so the word we takes in the word for at home

parts.note: taken as written
in means at home, as in staying in
the press is the newspapers collectively

explanation.surface: We drink at home while reading the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imbibe' puts IN inside WE to make WINE; 'with' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A winepress is the device that squeezes grapes to extract their juice for alcohol.

clue.text: River Severn starts in the United Kingdom

indicators.note: in places that opening letter inside the country's abbreviation

parts.note: UK is the abbreviation for the United Kingdom

indicators.note: starts means just the opening letter of the river's name is used

explanation.surface: A British river begins inside the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts' takes S from Severn; 'in' puts it inside UK. The Usk is a river in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: The Usk is a Welsh waterway flowing into the Severn estuary.

clue.text: Though about an expression of disgust

indicators.note: about means surrounding: the word though is around the answer's letters, at its end

explanation.surface: Someone sighs 'though' as a sign of revulsion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' says the word 'Though' surrounds the answer, which is its last three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The interjection people utter at something revolting, like yuck.

clue.text: I'm after a letter written by Kipling

indicators.note: after means the pronoun phrase comes behind the letter

parts.note: K is simply one letter of the alphabet
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone says they follow a message the author penned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a letter' here is any single letter; the answer fixes it as K. 'Letter' looks like correspondence.
explanation.definitionFit: Kim is the 1901 novel by Rudyard Kipling about an orphan boy in India.

clue.text: Setting up or breaking up a rising

indicators.note: breaking up the words a rising scatters their letters into a new order

explanation.surface: An uprising is either being organised or being crushed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking up' rearranges A RISING; 'or' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising a structure or fund is erecting or establishing it.

clue.text: Possibly flies in groups

parts.note: taken as written
sects are factions or groups, often religious

explanation.surface: Perhaps someone travels by air in parties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flies' looks like a verb but is a plural noun; 'Possibly' says they are an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Flies are one kind of six-legged creature, so they are examples.

clue.text: He's a lot on edge

parts.note: the pronoun he is taken as written; the 's is a link
M stands for a thousand in Roman numerals, a large number

explanation.surface: A man is very nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, hence 'a lot'; 'on' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A hem is the folded border of a piece of cloth.

clue.text: Hat and pipe mislaid-in the cemetery?

definitions.text: Hat and pipe mislaid-in the cemetery?

indicators.note: mislaid suggests the letters of hat and pipe are laid out wrongly, in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone has lost a hat and pipe, perhaps among the graves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mislaid' rearranges HAT and PIPE. The whole clue doubles as a hint: words found on a tombstone.
explanation.definitionFit: An epitaph is the inscription on a tombstone, found in a graveyard.

clue.text: Asked for breakfast in bed?

indicators.note: in places the morning food inside the word for a cot

parts.note: taken as written
an egg is a typical breakfast food

explanation.surface: Someone requested a morning meal served in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that breakfast stands for one of its items.
explanation.definitionFit: Begged means pleaded or requested earnestly.

clue.text: Make provision for books put aside

explanation.surface: Some books are set to one side while space is made for others.
explanation.definitionFit: To fit a room with racks for volumes; also to postpone a plan indefinitely.

clue.text: Is deep, perhaps, but may be detected

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the words is deep could be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: Someone profound may yet be found out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges IS DEEP; 'but may be' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Espied means caught sight of or spotted.

clue.text: Domestic storm centre

parts.note: a domestic is a household row; the idiom of a storm in a small china vessel describes a fuss over nothing

explanation.surface: The heart of a family quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: The British idiom 'a storm in a teacup' means a great fuss about something trivial.
explanation.definitionFit: The cup for drinking a hot brew is where, in the idiom, a trivial storm takes place.

clue.text: Seeing sense a prophet becomes a tourist

parts.note: sight is the sense of seeing
a seer is someone who foresees the future, a prophet

explanation.surface: A visionary gains insight and turns into a holidaymaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becomes' only links; 'a' sits beside the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A visitor who goes round looking at the notable places of a town.

clue.text: Drunken repast comes to a fine end

indicators.note: drunken suggests the letters of repast stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A boozy meal finishes splendidly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunken' rearranges REPAST. 'fine' means thin, not excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that narrows gradually to a point grows thinner towards its tip.

clue.text: Dog gets bit"—final news item

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them, to tail them
a piece is a bit or portion

explanation.surface: A dog bites someone, and that is the last story in the bulletin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog' looks like an animal but is the verb meaning follow; 'gets' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailpiece is something added at the end, such as a closing story in a newspaper.

clue.text: Stampede over the long grass

parts.note: on can mean over, as in a lid on a pot
a rush is a tall grasslike plant of marshes

explanation.surface: Cattle bolt across the tall pasture.
explanation.definitionFit: An onrush is a sudden forward surge, like a headlong charge of animals.

clue.text: Large troughs causing deep trouble amidships

indicators.note: amid means the jumbled letters go into the middle of the vessels word

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: trouble suggests the letters of deep are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: Big basins cause serious problems in the middle of a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amidships' splits as 'amid' plus 'ships'; 'trouble' turns DEEP into EEPD, set inside SHIPS after SH. Farmers dunk sheep in these baths to kill parasites.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheep dips are long baths of disinfectant through which a flock is driven.
